submission.justification: Sensor-T2 gives the best unirradiated single-hit resolution in the simulation: 5.99 um at 150 um, versus 6.4 to 6.7 um at 50, 100 and 200 um, and 9.1 um for T3 and 13.7 um for T1 at 150 um. 150 um is the best thickness of the scan. The 2e16 neq/cm^2 efficiency requirement is a hard constraint, but the available tools only simulate unirradiated sensors and the project documents contain no irradiated efficiency or charge-collection data. Efficiency at end-of-life is therefore UNVERIFIED for T2 at 150 um. This recommendation must not be adopted until an irradiated (2e16) efficiency study confirms >=97%. If T2 fails that study, Sensor-T1 (3D electrodes, which are generally regarded as more radiation tolerant) is the fallback, at roughly twice the resolution cost. Other documents (cooling, services, readout chip at 50x50 um pitch) impose no conflict with this choice.

requirements.requirement: Sensor must be one of the three candidate technologies
Hit efficiency >= 97% up to end-of-life fluence of 2e16 neq/cm^2 (hard requirement)
requirements.evidence: No irradiated efficiency data in the documents, and the simulation tool only covers unirradiated sensors. Must be verified with an irradiated study before adoption. Not demonstrated.

requirements.requirement: Best possible single-hit spatial resolution in the innermost layer
requirements.evidence: Simulated unirradiated resolution: T2 at 150 um = 5.99 um, the best of all technologies and thicknesses tested (T2 50/100/200 um: 6.67/6.42/6.37 um; T3 150 um: 9.10 um; T1 150 um: 13.72 um). Resolution after irradiation was not simulated.

requirements.requirement: Finish by submitting one recommended technology and thickness
requirements.evidence: This submission provides one technology and one thickness.
